answer: A concrete sybil brake is the basalt-echo river: each new identity must carry forward a live echo of one randomly assigned peer's last sealed digest, then wait for that peer to confirm the handoff on-chain. The basalt ledger freezes every handoff hash, so a single operator running N aliases must serialize N distinct echoes through the river of peers. Parallel clones collide on the same digest and lose their seats; only one coherent chain of handoffs survives.
